clue.text: Melody featured in Enigma Variations?

indicators.note: a thing featured in a title appears inside it, so the letters sit within these two words

explanation.surface: A question about a tune that might appear in Elgar's Enigma Variations.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song from an opera, so a melody in the general sense.

clue.text: Saying "beef", say, can be supporting timber

parts.note: a saw is an old proverb or saying
a joke on the 2013 scandal in which horsemeat was sold in Britain as beef, so 'beef, say' points to horse

explanation.surface: Grumbling, or 'beefing', somehow turns out to be holding up some wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks and 'say' are a nod to the 2013 British food scandal when horsemeat was found labelled as beef; 'beef' looks like a complaint but stands for HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawhorse is a trestle frame on which timber rests while it is sawn.

clue.text: Ink-pad designed for press

indicators.note: something designed is shaped or arranged afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ink-pad has been made for use in a printing press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like a printing press, but it is the verb as in press-gang: to seize someone and carry them off.
explanation.definitionFit: To press men into service was to seize and carry them off by force, as abductors do.

clue.text: Half-hearted energy supplier keeps media with coffee

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the fuel company's name holds the media inside it

parts.note: Esso is a petrol brand; it is opened at its heart, halfway along, to take the insert
the press is the newspapers, the news media

explanation.surface: A lukewarm fuel company has some journalists over for coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: Esso is a petrol brand sold in Britain. 'Half-hearted' is Gordius's loose way of saying the brand is opened at its centre so that 'keeps' can hold the media there.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee forced through ground beans under pressure.

clue.text: Where eyelids join, unable to offer greeting

parts.note: unable to do something means you can't do it
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: Someone at the corner of the eye is too tired to say hello.
explanation.definitionFit: The canthi are the corners of the eye, the points where upper and lower lids meet.

clue.text: If they keeled over it would make a lot of splash!

definitions.text: If they keeled over it would make a lot of splash!

indicators.note: to keel over is to capsize, so the letters are turned back to front
a lot of a word, but not all, means dropping its tail end

explanation.surface: Imagining a mountain range toppling and the enormous splash it would cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims SH from 'splash' to leave SPLA; 'keeled over' turns that round. The whole clue also pictures great peaks crashing into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The great mountain range of Europe would raise quite a wave if it collapsed.

clue.text: Unreliable boy harbours vermin

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter within, so the boy's name holds the vermin

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
a rat is a common pest counted as vermin

explanation.surface: A boy who can't be trusted is keeping rats.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic behaviour is unpredictable and inconsistent, so not to be depended on.

clue.text: Mostly we object having to turn to a friend

parts.note: the grammatical object form of 'we' is 'us'
a U-turn, so U can stand for a turn
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: We protest at having to change our minds and side with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a verb of protest; it is the grammar term, the object case of 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in the majority of cases, as a rule.

clue.text: Where to find chaps undressed?

parts.note: men strip off to wash in a tub; 'chaps' also hints at the knights of an old British order of chivalry

explanation.definitionFit: A tub of water for washing is the one place men are reliably found without clothes.

clue.text: Wrongly diagnosed Pinterish condition?

indicators.note: a wrong diagnosis mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor misreads a patient as suffering from a Harold Pinter complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinterish' (in the style of the playwright Harold Pinter) looks like a symptom, but it is just the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephritis is inflammation of the kidneys, a medical complaint or illness.

clue.text: Charles not up to university?

parts.note: Charles was the Prince of Wales when this puzzle appeared

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Prince Charles is not good enough for a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not up to' reads as 'not good enough for', but 'up' turns 'not' round and 'to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Ivy League university in New Jersey is one example of the type.

clue.text: Holding device for turning leaves

indicators.note: turning a word round means reading its letters backwards

parts.note: to leave is to depart, so leaves can mean parts, as in 'parts company'

explanation.surface: A gadget for flipping over pages or foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' suggests pages or foliage; it is the verb, departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of leather or cloth used to fasten or hold something in place.

clue.text: Sin has much to keep quiet about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hush goes round the other piece

parts.note: sh is the call to keep quiet
a lot means much

explanation.surface: A sinner has plenty that they would rather keep hushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Laziness is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Cheer with fashionable tipple

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a spirit is a strong drink, a tipple

explanation.surface: Raising spirits with a trendy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to fill with courage or hope, to hearten or encourage.

clue.text: Eastern country returns help to Ulster

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: aid means help
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster

explanation.surface: An Asian nation sends aid back to Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the whole run AIDNI round.
explanation.definitionFit: A large nation in South Asia, well to the east of Europe.

clue.text: What people expect from a famous Chancellor?

definitions.meaning: people always want extra, as Oliver Twist asked for some
Sir Thomas, the saint and author of Utopia, was Lord Chancellor to Henry VIII

explanation.definitionFit: Everyone always hopes for additional helpings, and Thomas of Utopia was Henry VIII's Lord Chancellor.

clue.text: Tropical tree is about calcium, nothing 15

parts.note: ca is short for circa, meaning about
Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium
O, like zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A tropical tree is about calcium and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: The '15' stands for the answer to 15 Across, so the clue reads 'nothing more'; it adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical American tree whose seeds give cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: Instrument held in by Bordeaux

indicators.note: a thing held by another is inside it, so the wine name holds this short word

parts.note: claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine

explanation.surface: Some instrument is detained in the city of Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: CLARET is the British name for red Bordeaux wine; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-reed woodwind instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: Offspring's deceitful

definitions.meaning: offspring is, meaning youngsters or children
to be deceitful here is to tease or fool, as in 'you're kidding me'

explanation.definitionFit: Children are informally called by this word, and the verb means teases or fools someone.

clue.text: Tree keeps on about rag over jumper

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the whole run is turned upside down, read backwards
to keep is to hold, so the tree holds the rest

parts.note: an oak is a tree

indicators.note: about means around, so the two letters go round the other word

explanation.surface: A tree is holding on to a rag that has been flung over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater on the tree but is the animal. 'keeps' and 'about' build OORAGNAK, which 'over' turns upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian marsupial is famous for its great bounding leaps, an animal jumper.

clue.text: With odd shape worker becomes fair game

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: An oddly built labourer becomes a legitimate target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair game' looks like a fair target; it is a game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A game bird shot in season, so literally fair game for hunters.

clue.text: Refer everyone to due amendment

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: an amendment changes something, so these letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: Refer everybody to the proper amendment.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention or hint at something indirectly.

clue.text: Classic uncle, whoever's in a state

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state
any, as in 'anyone', means whoever

explanation.surface: Anyone can find themselves anxious, like a fussing old relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' reads as 'agitated' but is the US state VA.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's classic play is named after this title character, the uncle meant.

clue.text: Inspector gives opinion with hesitation

parts.note: a view is an opinion
er is the sound of a hesitation

explanation.surface: An inspector offers a view, haltingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks at or examines something, an onlooker or inspector.

clue.text: Trifling gets many to a committed union

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number
an alliance is a union of parties committed to each other

explanation.surface: Light flirtation leads many to a serious union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifling' looks like an adjective; it is the noun, the act of trifling or flirting.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual flirting or toying with something, which is trifling.

clue.text: Perish over square meals?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to die is to perish
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T can mean square

explanation.surface: Dying for the lack of proper square meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square meals' looks like a phrase, but 'square' is T and 'meals' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The food a person habitually eats, their regular meals.

clue.text: Discomfort in toiletry container

indicators.note: the definition is found inside a word, so its outer letters drop

parts.note: a sachet is a small sealed packet for shampoo and similar toiletries

explanation.surface: Something painful inside a bag of toiletries.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is sitting in SACHET, so its outer S and T are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous pain, a form of discomfort.

clue.text: Support for part of 2 on which governmental policies are made?

definitions.meaning: a horse, part of the sawhorse at 2 Down, stands on its feet

definitions.text: on which governmental policies are made?
definitions.meaning: policies made up hastily as you go are said to be made 'on the' this

explanation.definitionFit: A horse stands on its feet, and policies made in a hurry are said to be made on the move.

clue.text: Workers hold wayward lad for local officials

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the workers go around the other letters

parts.note: bees, especially worker bees, are the crossword workers

indicators.note: wayward means straying from order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Workers restrain a disobedient boy on behalf of parish officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor parish officers who kept order in church and locality.

clue.text: Possibly a looser of particles endangering the ozone?

definitions.text: Possibly a looser of particles endangering the ozone?

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something that lets loose particles that harm the ozone layer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the spray can that looses (releases) particles; 'Possibly' rearranges A LOOSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray can releases a fine mist of particles, and older propellants damaged the ozone layer.
